title: When God Feels Silent: 5 Reasons, 5 Steps
hook: If heaven feels quiet, you’re not abandoned—start here.
script: If heaven feels quiet, you’re not abandoned—start here. Sometimes God is waiting for the right time (Hab 2:3). Sometimes He is growing your endurance (James 1:2–4). Sometimes there’s too much noise, and you need the quiet Jesus chose (Luke 5:16). Sometimes He invites a heart check (Psalm 139:23). And sometimes He’s redirecting you to a better path (Acts 16:6–10). What now? Lament honestly with Psalm 13. Obey the last clear thing He told you. Sit in five minutes of silence daily. Invite wise counsel (Proverbs 11:14). And keep knocking like Luke 18. Silence can shape you, not break you.

title: When God is Quiet: From Ache to Action
hook: If God feels silent right now, watch this.
script: If God feels silent right now, watch this. Delay isn’t denial; His promise has a schedule (Hab 2:3). Trials train muscles you can’t see yet (James 1:2–4). Volume kills voice, so withdraw like Jesus did (Luke 5:16). Ask God to search your motives (Psalm 139:23). And stay open if He’s steering you elsewhere (Acts 16:6–10). Try this today: Pray Psalm 13 out loud. Do the last instruction you’re sure about. Practice a daily quiet five. Seek a mature friend for counsel (Proverbs 11:14). Pray persistently like the widow in Luke 18. Then whisper, Jesus, what are You inviting me to do next?

title: The Silent 5: A 7-Day Reset with God
hook: You need to hear this today: silence isn’t absence; it’s invitation.
script: You need to hear this today: silence isn’t absence; it’s invitation. God’s quiet can be timing, training, too much noise, a heart check, or redirection. But you’re not stuck. For seven days, try the Silent 5. Sit still for five minutes. Breathe a simple prayer: Speak, Lord, I’m listening. Ask two questions: What did You highlight today? What step of obedience is next? Read Psalm 13, then do one small act from yesterday’s light. Text a trusted believer for wisdom (Proverbs 11:14). Keep asking like Luke 18. Over time you’ll notice Isaiah 30:21 happening—a steady voice guiding your steps.
